editorial.headline: Religious Junior Secondary Education, With a Clear PMA Position
editorial.standfirst: This religious junior-secondary education activity is open to 100% foreign ownership nationally and is not moratorium-blocked in Bali, subject to verification for the specific address.
editorial.body:
KBLI 85314 covers junior-secondary education for learners aged 13–15, together with related equivalency education, oriented around Protestant, Catholic, Hindu, Buddhist or Confucian religious studies. Its curriculum reaches beyond general religious instruction: sacred texts, worship law and practice, classical religious languages, and the history of religious civilisation and figures all sit within its stated scope. At the same time, it retains general knowledge and skills learning. The examples named in the record range from Christian theology and Catholic religious junior-secondary schools to madyama widyalaya, madyama widya pasraman and muda dhammasekha.

This is therefore the activity for an operator delivering a defined form of faith-oriented junior-secondary schooling, rather than a narrow class in a single tradition. The scope is specific about the learning offered and the age group served, while still recognising related equivalency education. It is equally specific that religious learning does not displace general knowledge and skills. The record does not list any business-scale categories as open to the activity. No scale designation should be assumed beyond that absence.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is open. The stated foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, meaning the activity may be fully foreign-owned at the national level. That is the central ownership fact: there is no lower national cap stated for this code. The record identifies Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021 as its PMA source, anchoring the national position without adding conditions that are not supplied here.

Bali requires a more location-conscious reading, but not a false alarm. The Bali status is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. For this activity, the record places it in the medium-high/high-risk range and says it is not blocked by the moratorium; verification remains required for the particular address. In practical terms, Bali does not impose a moratorium block on PMA registration for this activity on the facts given. Nor does the Bali reason state a separate foreign-ownership percentage or partnership condition, so none should be implied.
